criteria.descriptor: Full marks: assigns correct, real mechanisms to each artefact type — git/commit-hash for code and prompt, content-addressed data versioning (DVC/git-LFS/lakeFS) for large data with a git pointer, a pinned immutable model snapshot or model registry with decoding params, and a versioned eval config — and correctly states that immutable content-addressed hashes (not mutable tags/aliases) are what make a run reproducible. Deduct for wrong claims such as 'put the eval set and index in git', treating a moving alias as reproducible, or omitting decoding params/embedding version.

Full marks: addresses all four required parts — per-artefact versioning for all five types, a per-run manifest tying a score to exact inputs, a manifest-diff/ablation diagnosis of THIS regression, and CI/CD integration (PR eval gate plus scheduled drift eval). Deduct for each part missing or left generic (e.g. no run manifest, or CI mentioned only as a one-time gate with no scheduled eval for moving hosted models).

Full marks: justifies choices by mechanism — why git is unsuitable for large binaries, why a silently-rolled alias produces a regression with no deploy, why immutability/content-addressing enables replay — and reasons through the diagnosis and at least one explicit trade-off rather than listing tools. Deduct when claims are asserted without cause-and-effect reasoning.

Full marks: well-structured (e.g. per-artefact then manifest then diagnosis then CI/CD), uses correct vocabulary (content-addressed, manifest/lockfile, pinned snapshot, registry alias, ablation) precisely, and stays within a focused length. Deduct for disorganised, rambling, or jargon-dropping-without-meaning answers.

expected_answer_points: Version each of the five artefact types with an appropriate mechanism: code and prompts in git by commit/hash, large data (eval set, corpus, index) via content-addressed storage (DVC/git-LFS/lakeFS) with a pointer in git, model pinned in config or a model registry, and eval config as its own versioned artefact.

Replace the moving model alias "gpt-4o" with a pinned/dated immutable snapshot and record decoding parameters (temperature, top_p, seed, max_tokens), because a silently-rolled alias changes outputs with no code deploy.

Stop mutating datasets and prompts in place (CSV appended in Drive, prompt pasted from Notion); make artefacts immutable and content-addressed so an append or edit produces a new version rather than overwriting.

Emit a per-run manifest/lockfile that links the score to exact versions (git SHA, prompt hash, model id+params, dataset hash, embedding/index version, eval-harness version, environment/container digest) in an experiment tracker so any run is reproducible.

Diagnose the regression by diffing the two runs' manifests and doing one-artefact-at-a-time ablation, identifying the likely causes (alias roll, mutated eval CSV, re-embedded index) rather than blaming application code.
Include the embedding model and RAG index version as part of reproducibility, and version the eval harness plus any LLM-as-judge model and judge prompt.

Wire evals into CI as a gate on every relevant PR (run against a pinned dataset, fail on regression beyond tolerance vs baseline) and keep a scheduled/nightly eval to catch drift from moving hosted dependencies without a deploy; promote via registry aliases and support rollback.
Name an explicit trade-off, e.g. pinned snapshots (reproducible but need migration) vs moving aliases (auto-updated but non-reproducible), or prompt-as-code vs prompt-registry.
common_pitfalls: Proposes 'version everything in git' and misses that git handles large eval datasets and RAG indexes poorly, so binary/data artefacts need content-addressed external storage (DVC/git-LFS/lakeFS) with only a pointer in git.
Leaves the model as the moving alias "gpt-4o" and never recognises that a silent provider roll changes outputs with no deploy, so misdiagnoses the regression as an application-code bug.
Versions only the prompt and model name while forgetting decoding params (temperature, seed), the embedding model, and the RAG index version — all of which affect outputs and reproducibility.
Versions each artefact in isolation but never introduces a per-run manifest/lockfile, so a score still cannot be traced back to the exact inputs that produced it.
Adds a one-time CI eval gate on PRs but omits a scheduled/nightly eval, missing that moving hosted-model dependencies drift and regress without any deploy to trigger CI.

Confuses mutable tags/aliases with immutable content-addressed versions — e.g. reusing the same dataset name after appending rows, or promoting by editing production directly instead of a registry alias.
reference_answer:
Versioning per artefact type. Code and prompts belong in git by commit SHA: promote the prompt from a Notion copy-paste to prompt-as-code — a reviewed, diff-able file (or a prompt registry entry) with an immutable version/hash. Large data (eval sets, RAG corpus, index) is a poor fit for git; use content-addressed data versioning (DVC, git-LFS, or lakeFS) that stores an immutable hash/pointer in git while the blob lives in object storage. Extend DVC to cover the eval CSV, not just the corpus, and never mutate in place — appending rows must mint a new dataset version. The model must be pinned to an immutable dated snapshot, not the moving alias "gpt-4o"; self-hosted or fine-tuned models go in a model registry (MLflow/W&B) by version. Crucially, pin decoding params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, seed) and the embedding-model + index version too — they change outputs. Eval config (harness code, metric/threshold definitions, and any LLM-judge model + judge prompt) is itself a versioned artefact.

Run manifest. Every eval run and production inference emits an immutable manifest recording git SHA, prompt hash, model id + params, dataset hash, embedding/index version, eval-harness version, and the environment/container digest, stored in an experiment tracker keyed to the score. Content-addressed hashes (not mutable tags) make a run replayable.

Diagnosis. Diff the 0.91 and 0.78 manifests. With no code deploy, the culprits surface: "gpt-4o" silently rolled to a new snapshot, the eval CSV was mutated (new dataset hash), and the index was re-embedded. Attribute the delta by ablation — hold four artefacts fixed and swap one at a time.

CI/CD. Run the suite on a pinned dataset version on every PR touching code/prompt/eval; fail the build on regression beyond tolerance versus a baseline. Because hosted models move without a deploy, keep the scheduled eval as a drift alarm. Promote via registry aliases (dev→staging→prod) instead of editing prod, and enable rollback to a known-good manifest bundle.

Trade-off: pinned snapshots give reproducibility but demand active migration before deprecation; prompt-as-code gains review and atomic coupling at the cost of non-engineers editing more slowly.
